slot.brief: Write the balanced combustion equation of a gaseous fuel, count Δng, and convert the given ΔH to ΔU (or vice versa) using ΔngRT.

stem: For complete combustion of $1$ mol of propane, with water formed as a liquid, find $\\Delta U$ at $300$ K if $\Delta H=-2200$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. Take $R=8.0$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O(l), so Δn_gas = 3 − 6 = −3. Using ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gasRT, ΔU = −2200 − (−3)(8)(300)/1000 = −2192.8 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$\text{C}_3\text{H}_8(g)+5\text{O}_2(g)\rightarrow3\text{CO}_2(g)+4\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
$\Delta n_g=3-6=-3$
$RT=(8.0)(300)=2400$ J mol$^{-1}=2.4$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\Delta H=\Delta U+\Delta n_gRT$
$\Delta U=-2200-(-3)(2.4)=-2192.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

Independent check: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O(l), so Δn_gas = 3 − 6 = −3. Using ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gasRT, ΔU = −2200 − (−3)(8)(300)/1000 = −2192.8 kJ mol⁻¹.
